summary: Apache-Sitgreaves NF lookout; 1933 Aermotor MC-24 tower, 1965 or early-1970s 54-ft rebuild; destroyed in the June 2011 Wallow Fire; NHLR-registered 2009.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-24 (1933); 54-ft steel K-Brace tower with CL-100 cab (1965 or early-1970s rebuild)
facts.status_note: NHLR and Peakbagging say destroyed in the June 2011 Wallow Fire; Forest Lookouts says extensive damage

events.note: Fifty-foot lookout tower and ranger's cabin reported on the summit in a January 9, 1914 newspaper item; the item does not give a build date
On June 23, 1915, St. Johns Boy Scouts climbed the fifty-foot tower while Forest officers explained the fire-locating method
Aermotor MC-24 tower constructed; NHLR gives 1933 as the build year of a 54-foot tower
54-foot steel K-Brace tower with CL-100 cab built to replace the earlier structure; Peakbagging dates the rebuild to the early 1970s
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on September 2, 2009
Wallow Fire swept over Escudilla Mountain on June 6, 2011
Tower destroyed in the June 2011 Wallow Fire per NHLR and Peakbagging; Forest Lookouts says extensive damage

evidence.supports: Location within the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests

evidence.quote: Escudilla Lookout was destroyed in the Wallow Fire in June 2011

corrections.why: NHLR and Peakbagging both say the tower was destroyed in the June 2011 Wallow Fire. Forest Lookouts describes only extensive damage, so the record should not say standing.

corrections.proposed: Aermotor MC-24 (1933 tower); 54-ft steel K-Brace with CL-100 cab (1965 or early 1970s rebuild)
corrections.why: Forest Lookouts ties the Aermotor MC-24 to 1933. Forest Lookouts and Peakbagging both say the 54-foot tower came in a later rebuild, while NHLR credits the 54-foot CL-100 tower to 1933.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts describes extensive damage, while NHLR and Peakbagging say the tower was destroyed. The record uses destroyed because two sources agree and the fire date matches.

notes_for_editor: Status corrected from standing to destroyed. Unresolved: the 54-ft rebuild date (1965 per Forest Lookouts, early 1970s per Peakbagging) and destroyed vs extensive damage in the 2011 fire. Two WMI Central fetches returned HTTP 429 and were not read. A Facebook search snippet says the tower is no longer staffed; not fetched, so not used. Staffing and current access are unknown; no access level is set. The brief lists Escudilla Peak Lookout as another name and says the records share a register number; no fetched page uses that name, and NHLR assigns US 826 to this lookout.
